correctness.rationale: Writing Q=a(x²+y²)+xy, the radial identity is d(r²−1)/dt=−2Q(r²−1), and the on-circle angular equation is Q−sin²θ=(a−1/2)+R cos(2θ−φ). For b>R it has a constant sign; integrating inverse speed gives least orbit period 2π/Δ. The observable e^{2iθ} itself has half that period, consistent with frequency spacing 2Δ. After the respective shifts of v=2θ−φ, its Ode is v̇=2ε(b−R cos v). Writing h=tan(v/2) gives ḣ=ε[(b−R)+(b+R)h²]; scaling h by β=sqrt((b−R)/(b+R)) and taking arctangent gives uniform phase ẇ=εΔ modulo π. Consequently ζ=e^{2iw} is uniform under physical-time sampling, and U=−ε e^{iφ}(ζ+k)/(1+kζ), with k=(1−β)/(1+β)=R/(b+Δ). Expanding the Möbius factor, the constant coefficient is k and nonzero centered coefficients are (1−k²)(−k)^{j−1}, times the unit-modulus prefactor. Orthogonality squares their moduli in the centered covariance and gives exactly the claimed one-sided atoms and correlation with the stated Fourier convention. Their total mass is 1−k². With p=1−k²=2Δ/(b+Δ), the variance-normalized frequency is ε(b+Δ)pJ where J has geometric(p) law on the positive integers. The exact geometric tail gives pJ⇒Exp(1), hence the signed scale εR and the characteristic-function limit. The unnormalized mass tends to zero and neither endpoint is a periodic parameter. The form-feed typo in the displayed period line of the proof does not affect the correctly stated result or the integral evaluation.

value.rationale: The doubled-angle observable is the natural complex coordinate on the antipodal phase quotient. Its exact covariance and full signed power give a useful temporal invariant beyond one-time angular statistics or the period. They quantify a concrete singular effect: every fixed harmonic collapses toward zero frequency as the period diverges, but increasing harmonic indices on the variance scale retain a nondegenerate distribution at physical frequencies of order R. The endpoint sign and scale and the vanishing raw variance distinguish this from merely interpolating a line spectrum or tabulating phase densities.
residual_risks: A narrow deterministic observable result, not a classification of generic slow-gate spectra, limit-cycle stability, or spectra of perturbations off the orbit.
